rates.status: MEASURED CO-RUN. T_G co-run = 0.1474 s/block (median of 25 base-block samples, 99.8% of GPU-time overlapping NPU executes; same-session solo 0.1600); T_N co-run = 0.6484 s/block (9 GEMMs at 0.3904 under GPU load + 0.2580 downsep). Sustained-run check PASSES (tools/npu/sustain_npu.py, capture sustain_npu_20261115_214149, docs/device/RESULTS_sustain_npu.md): 60 rounds x 9 GEMMs = 24.6 s of continuous TPU work, drift +0.35% (first-20% 408.902 ms vs last-20% 410.346 ms per round; slope +0.03 ms/round; TPU zone 25.0 -> 31.0 C) => no throttling over a full NPU stage, so T_N needs no derating term. Still TBD: ffn.down under contention (0.2580 s is solo - corun holds only the 9 block GEMMs), and the decode's CONV_2D class (10.554 s) was not soaked for 23.5 s. Per-tensor-scale parity is MEASURED (2.15x mean GEMM error, 6/40 Gate-1 cosine failures) - see gate_4_parity and docs/device/RESULTS_scales.md.

rates.T_V_conv_tpu_status: COMPLETE gate-compliant measured sum over 100% of the decode conv MACs, as kT shifted 2-D CONV_2D taps, one execute per frame per tap (batch>1 will not compile above ~1 MB/frame). Sweep start TPU 32.0 C vs a 32.1 C battery+3 gate (PASS, confirmed on a second sample); the two dominant classes (68% of MACs) ran at that floor. T_V_s_per_chunk is now SET: the mid-block 3-D attention was subsequently measured (32.38 GMAC: 0.601 s on the TPU vs 0.0855 s on Mali, 7.0x), so the decode is complete in all three configurations (10.640 hybrid / 11.155 all-TPU / 12.342 all-Mali). Hot control run (18:17): 11.412 s -> the cool run is 7.5% faster. Evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_vae_tv.md, conv_sweep_20261115_182512.json, attn_tv_20261115_211944.json.
rates.T_V_conv_tpu_note: CONV_2D reaches 719-2024 GOPS on this HAL on the gate-compliant run (685-1842 on the hot control) vs 285 GOPS for FULLY_CONNECTED: the Edge TPU is a conv engine and the DiT block's 10 GEMMs are being served by the wrong op class. Worth testing ffn.up/attn as 1x1 CONV_2D before accepting the 4.18x T_N/T_G penalty as silicon.
rates.T_V_engine_convention_note: The GOPS columns in RESULTS_vae_tv.md are NOT on the same basis. The TPU numbers (969.7 aggregate, 2024 best class) are FLOP/s = 2xMAC/s. The Mali class column (378-486) and its 417.5 aggregate are MAC/s. Like-for-like Mali is 835.1 FLOP-GOPS, so the TPU is 1.161x faster at the decode - identical to the time ratio 12.256/10.554, which is the number to quote. On that basis the Mali conv kernel runs at 95.2% of Mali's own 877 FLOP-GOPS GEMM rate (47.2% of the 1770 peak), NOT the '48% of the GEMM rate' stated in RESULTS_vae_tv.md section 6 - 48% looks like percent-of-peak. Consequence: the 'halo-staged activation tile, 871 GOPS ceiling' next action assumes ~2x headroom that this arithmetic does not support; residual headroom is ~5% aggregate, ~14% on the best class.

cut.formula: period(k_b) = max(k_b*T_G, (B-k_b)*T_N + T_V); k* = (B*T_N + T_V)/(T_N + T_G)
cut.B_note: 6 denoising steps x 30 DiT blocks per 9-frame chunk (docs/00_START_HERE.md, docs/02_model_spec.md). The formula needs B and it existed only in prose.
cut.k_b_solo_estimate_note: Solo-rate cross-check of the solved k_b=160 (not the number of record). With B=180, T_G=0.1618, T_V=10.554 and all-TPU T_N=0.6758: k* = 157.8 blocks (87.7% on Mali), both sides balance at 25.54 s against 39.68 s for all-180-blocks-plus-decode serial on Mali -> 1.55x. With the hybrid T_N=0.4651 (ffn.down on Mali): k* = 150.4 (83.5%), period 24.33 s, 1.63x. The co-run pair supersedes this; the two agree within 1.3% on k_b.
cut.next_measurement_priority: Sustained throttling is RETIRED for the cool regime: a 60-round / 24.6 s continuous soak (tools/npu/sustain_npu.py) drifted +0.35% (first-20% 408.902 ms vs last-20% 410.346 ms per round, slope +0.03 ms/round) with the TPU zone at 25.0 -> 31.0 C, so T_N carries no derating term. What remains: (a) ffn.down (0.2580 of the 0.6484) is still solo - corun holds only the 9 block GEMMs; (b) the decode's CONV_2D class (10.554 s) was not soaked; (c) the soak topped out at 31 C whereas the same GEMM workload has been measured heating TPU 29 -> 59 C in 54 s, so a warm 200-chunk pipeline (P3.1) can still reach a regime no soak has covered. Off the rate path entirely: Gate 1's PSNR/SSIM leg is runnable now (.venv-ref, torch 2.15.0+cpu), which also arms Gate 4's frame parity.
cut.status: SOLVED from co-run rates: k_b = 160 (GPU blocks [0,160), NPU [160,180) then the decode), period 23.61 s = max(23.58 GPU, 23.61 NPU) with the hybrid T_V = 10.640, idle 0.02 s, 5.394x against NPU-only (127.35 s). Cross-check with the conservative solo pair (T_G 0.1618, T_N 0.6758): k* = 157.8, period 25.54 s, i.e. the two agree within 1.3% on k_b. Sensitivity: step-level granularity (k_b multiple of L=30) forces k_b=150 and costs 27.3%; ignoring T_V when solving puts k_b at 147 and costs 36.5% once the decode is paid serially. T_V is complete in all three engine splits and the 24.6 s soak showed no derating, so the only open item above this number is ffn.down measured solo rather than under contention.

gate_4_parity.status: FAILS on device, and the failure is structural: only 25.8% of each [384,1536] TPU output tile is bit-exact against an exact host reference
gate_4_parity.targets: per-block cosine >= 0.999 vs FP32; frame PSNR >= 28 dB, SSIM >= 0.92
gate_4_parity.evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_gate3_parity.md + tools/pipe/gate3_parity.py (commit b5f26c2). Host reference is exact by construction: fp32 BLAS with K-split partials < 2^24, accumulated int64, requantised clamp(round(acc/127)), validated against brute-force int64 including the all -128 worst case. GEMM-level cosine from RESULTS_scales.md (40/40 per-column pass) still stands for the WEIGHTS; this is the DEVICE OUTPUT that fails.
gate_4_parity.failure_structure: The exact region is tile-aligned, not scattered: the last 384-column block is exact for EVERY row (384x384 = 147,456 elements = 25.00% of the tile) and row 0 is exact for every column (1,536 = 0.26%) -> 25.26% predicted against 25.8% measured. ffn.up: 22 of 24 blocks at 1.4%, then 45% and 92%. A numerics error would not align to a 384-column boundary and a row boundary; a partial-writeback bug does. That is evidence, not proof, for writeback over compute.
gate_4_parity.ruled_out_by_measurement: async write (150 ms re-dump identical), 4096-aligned buffer (bit-identical), transpose, row stride, row/column permutation, n-shift, stale other-GEMM data, weight-byte echo. The bit-exact regions prove the host reference is right, so the break is on the device side.
gate_4_parity.open_discriminator: Whether the TPU COMPUTES only what it writes (true rate ~56 GOPS, T_N ~4x worse = ~2.6 s/block, thesis inverted) or computes everything and writes back a quarter (rates stand, only the dump path is broken). This is now the highest-priority question in the project - above the GPU derate - because a 4x optimistic T_N would invalidate every NPU rate in this lock. CHEAPEST DECISIVE TEST, before any bisect: scale N at fixed M,K (384 / 768 / 1152 / 1536) and watch the wall time. Flat time = only one column block is computed; linear time = the compute is real and the writeback is the bug. One run, one variable, prices the whole risk.

gate_5_memory.method_finding: smaps_rollup reported 85,137 kB for proc_a where dumpsys reported 249,290 kB - a 2.93x UNDER-REPORT. The missing 164,153 kB is the 'GL mtrack' row: Mali driver CL memory that smaps never sees. proc_b, which has no GL mtrack, agrees between the two sources to 0.1% and is the control proving the gap is driver memory rather than a sampling artefact. Every future memory claim must come from dumpsys/GL mtrack: a smaps-only number would have passed this gate on 24% of the true footprint.
gate_5_memory.hygiene: The first attempt FAILED honestly: the device still held a second 46,399,488 B copy of the block (hv_block_int8.bin, T_N era) plus stale weight scratch, all removed before the passing run; npu_block must re-push its blobs. NOTE the freed-byte figure does not reconcile - 46,399,488 + 128 MiB = 180,617,216 B, but the report quotes 137,502,720 B freed, which implies 86.9 MiB of scratch, not 128 MiB. One of those three numbers is wrong; re-measure before quoting it.
gate_5_memory.gate_numbering: This is GATE 5 (memory). The commit title and the RESULTS file call it Gate 4 - the labels are swapped in the docs. Gate 3 = thermal, Gate 4 = parity, Gate 5 = memory; the same mix-up labels the outstanding parity work as 'Gate 3'.

phase3_pipeline._comment: Build order: phase3_pipeline/PLAN.md. P3.1 measured 2026-11-15 22:03 -> docs/device/RESULTS_handoff_p31.md
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_handoff: PASS - two-process MAP_SHARED two-slot ring, 200 chunks: 0 mismatching words of 587,520/chunk, 200/200 in order, t_cons > t_prod on 400/400 publishes. Ring file 9,408,512 B = PAGE (4096-B header page: seq/done per slot) + 2 x SLOT_STRIDE (4,702,208 = 4,700,160 payload rounded up to a page) - exactly two slots, which a third buffer would have exposed as a size mismatch. Split --role producer / --role consumer from two separate adb sessions passed 30/30 with stream_done=1 - the shape P3.2/P3.3 will use.
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_latency: publish->consume 680.9 us mean / 661.7 median / 1023 max free-running; 2541.4 mean / 8167 max with a 1 ms consumer stall. msync(4 KiB, MS_SYNC) median 63.7 us (mean 88.9) = 0.0004% of a 23.61 s chunk, so the pessimistic barrier is affordable and there is no case for MS_ASYNC.
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_decision_input: Back-pressure is the NORMAL path: the producer blocked on 198/200 chunks even free-running, because writing 4.7 MB costs ~0.15 ms while the consumer's verify pass costs ~0.6 ms. So the second slot is required, not an optimisation - a one-slot ring serialises the test into 200 x (write + read).
phase3_pipeline.payload_tokens_note: The ring carries M = 1530 tokens (3 latent frames x 510) x d 1536 in fp16 = 4,700,160 B = 4.48 MiB. T_G was measured at exactly M=1530, and T_N's 4 x 384 = 1536 token tiles cover 1530 with padding, so the solved rates apply to the real chunk without a token-count correction.
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_not_established: No period, overlap or CPU-time split (P3.4/P3.5); nothing about the INT8 weight artifact (the ring carries the fp16 residual for the test); one-slot starvation behaviour unmeasured. Correctness test only - thermal was recorded (TPU 25.0 -> 25.0 C, battery 21.8 -> 21.8 C), not gated.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_gpu_stage: PASS on correctness, with a 32% cost that is now a DECISION, not a detail (docs/device/RESULTS_proc_a_p32.md, commits fc15363/9f52635). Same binary, real artifacts/blocks/block_00.bin, 8 blocks per route: route B (file mmap + clImportMemoryARM) gives 10/10 weights zero-copy, 80/80 GEMMs, 8/8 chunks drained by a second PID.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_zero_copy_cost: ZERO-COPY IS NOT FREE ON THE GPU STAGE: import 214.5 ms/block (661.9 GOPS) vs device-local staging 162.2 ms/block (875.4 GOPS, reproducing the 161.8 ms benchmark). +32.2%. The penalty tracks the weight working set - both FFN planes (13.8 MB each) go +15/+16%, attention only +4% - so it is per-byte cost, not per-import overhead.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_cut_consequence_not_applied: k_b* 157 with period 25.55 s (staging) / k_b* 148 with period 31.75 s (import), against the locked 160 / 23.61 s. Reported, NOT applied: k_b stays 160 until the one-copy-vs-speed decision below is taken.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_open_decision: ONE INT8 COPY vs GPU SPEED. The project premise is a single copy shared by both engines; zero-copy import costs 32% of the GPU stage, and staging to device-local memory recovers it only by making a second copy. Both branches are measured (25.55 s vs 31.75 s period), so this is now the student's call. UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS worth one experiment first: on a unified-memory SoC the Mali GPU and the CPU share the same LPDDR4X, so a 32% per-byte penalty is more consistent with a cache-attribute/mapping effect in clImportMemoryARM (uncached or write-through mapping) than with bandwidth physics - the working-set scaling fits that reading. Route A (AHardwareBuffer, which Gate 2 verified also imports) and/or different import hints are the cheap tests; if either recovers the 32%, the one-copy premise survives at full speed.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_not_in_any_period_yet: Host-side payload conversion costs 44-57 ms/block and is NOT in either period above; it is removable with an fp16 epilogue kernel, so no corrected period is quoted until that exists. Attention/softmax/AdaLN are still outside the stage. Both runs started 0.3-0.9 C over the battery+3 line on the idle floor (floor-grade, recorded).
phase3_pipeline.p3_3_npu_stage: PASS - proc_b runs the real artifact: one createFromFd view of block_00.bin with per-GEMM setOperandValueFromMemory windows (so still ONE stored INT8 copy), 9 held one-op graphs compiling in 4.52 s. 9-GEMM stage 377.8 ms/block = 264.3 GOPS, i.e. 0.9677x the co-run 390.4 ms the cut was solved with; three runs 373.4-381.1 ms (2.06% spread, no thermal trend). 108/108 executes (3 chunks x 4 tiles x 9 GEMMs), 3/3 chunks consumed, producer->consumer payload hash chain MATCH, 0 NaN words. Evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_proc_b_p33.md, commits e44e086/549a8d6.
phase3_pipeline.p3_3_down_projection: ffn.down on real weights, same harness: TPU 7xK=1280+6xADD = 272.3 ms/block vs Mali 47.33 ms -> 5.75x slower, confirming the synthetic finding on the real artifact. The TPU branch needs a 13,762,560 B weight repack, which breaks the one-copy rule - reported, NOT adopted.
phase3_pipeline.p3_3_arithmetic_gap: The two whole-block figures do not share a baseline: 656.8 - 272.3 = 384.5 ms and 388.1 - 47.33 = 340.8 ms imply 9-GEMM stages 12.8% apart, and NEITHER is the 377.8 ms measured in this run - both come from the `stage` run that started 4.1 C over the gate. Honest whole-block numbers from this run: 650.1 ms with TPU down, 425.1 ms with Mali down. The quoted 5.75x is a down-projection-only ratio and is correct; the whole-block pair needs re-basing on one run before it enters the paper.
phase3_pipeline.p3_3_split_block_issue: A block split across engines (9 GEMMs on the NPU, ffn.down on Mali) consumes GPU time INSIDE the NPU stage. The locked cut formula period = max(k*T_G, (B-k)*T_N + T_V) assumes each block belongs wholly to one engine and has no term for that. With Mali-down the whole NPU block is 425.1 ms against the cut's T_N of 648.4 ms (which assumes down on the TPU at 258.0 ms): the pipeline as built is faster per NPU block but steals GPU time. Settle this in P3.4/P3.5 - do not edit T_N to fit it.
phase3_pipeline.p3_3_not_established: Parity (Gate 3) unmeasured; the decode is a stub citing T_V = 10.640 s; steady-state period is P3.5. fp16->INT8 payload quantisation is 5.3-13.8 ms/chunk, and the later-chunk 391-710 ms queue is the back-pressure P3.1 identified, not handoff cost.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_coordinator: PASS in both configurations (docs/device/RESULTS_stream_p34.md, commit 471b102). 4 chunks x 1 NPU block: 4/4 published, 4/4 consumed, 144/144 executes (4x4x9), GPU block 187.2 ms median with 10 closures / 168.0 ms with one, NPU block 385.9 ms, first handoff 0.244 us. 2 chunks x 20 NPU blocks - the cut's real stage: 40 blocks, 386.6 ms median, chunk windows 9.34 / 9.25 s, 1440/1440 executes (2x20x4x9). Both captures started 1.8 / 3.7 C over the gate, so this is comparison-grade, not table-grade; the decode is still a cited 10.640 s stub.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_launch_order_is_correctness: Both binaries reset_headers() when they map the ring, so a consumer that maps late WIPES a producer's publish and the run dies 300 s later as chunk_never_published. The runner now waits for the consumer's READY before starting the producer. That is a correctness dependency, not a convenience: a refactor that reorders the launch reintroduces a failure that presents as a hang. It deserves a test that fails on the wrong order, because nothing else in the harness would catch it.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_handoff_granularity: proc_a publishes per BLOCK, while the cut hands off once per 160 blocks (the GPU prefix). In the 2x20 run the GPU therefore did 0.214 s of work while the NPU ran 18.4 s -> 1.1% overlap: the schedule being measured was not the schedule the cut describes. Fix queued: --pub-every N on proc_a. Until it lands, no overlap or period number from this harness speaks to the locked 160/23.61 s.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_verifier_overhead: The P3.3 correctness harness FNV-hashes ffn.up's 13,762,560 B output on EVERY block at ~170 MB/s = ~81 ms/block: 1.62 s per 20-block chunk (17.3% of the 9.34 s window, and 13.0 s at 160 blocks). It is a harness cost, not pipeline cost - and the fix should make the verifier CHEAP (strided hash, or a word-wise/vectorised FNV) rather than switch it off. The '0 mismatching words / 0 NaN' guarantee is what makes the stage numbers believable, and it is about to be traded away for speed.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_reporting_gap: The 4x1 utilisation line cannot be checked as written: 'both engines busy together 630.6 ms = 39.4% NPU busy, 70.5% GPU busy' is self-contradictory on its face, because an engine busy for 385.9 ms cannot be co-busy for 630.6 ms. 630.6 must be the UNION of the two busy intervals, and the wall time the percentages are relative to is never stated. Report wall, union and each engine's own busy time as separate numbers.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_tg_is_stale: The locked T_G = 0.1474 s/block came from the synthetic LCG blob co-run. On the real artifact it is 0.1622 (P3.2, staged), 0.1680 (P3.4 pipeline, one closure) or 0.1872 (P3.4, 10 per-GEMM closures). Re-solving with the locked T_N and T_V: period 25.48 / 26.21 / 28.53 s and k_b* 157.1 / 156.0 / 152.4 - all ABOVE the locked 23.59 s. So the locked period is not achievable as built: P3.5 must be scored against a re-solved cut, not against 23.61 s, and T_G should be re-locked to the real-artifact value once the 2x2 below picks it. The NPU side moves the other way - 20 blocks cost 7.73 s measured (385.9 ms each, down on Mali) against 12.97 s modelled - so the GPU prefix is now the binding side.
phase3_pipeline.p3_4_import_penalty_unreconciled: P3.2 put zero-copy import at 214.5 ms vs staged 162.2 ms (+32%), and that figure framed the one-copy-vs-speed decision. P3.4's pipeline measures 187.2 ms on the SAME import route - 12.7% faster than P3.2 - with a one-closure reference at 168.0 ms, so the implied import penalty in the pipeline is ~11%, not 32%. The doc attributes the 187.2 vs 147.4 gap to 'the import penalty and the closure overhead' without separating them. Before that decision is taken, run the 2x2: {import, staging} x {1 closure, 10 closures}. It separates the two causes and may delete the decision entirely.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5a_measured_period: THE PIPELINE'S PERIOD IS NOW MEASURED, AND IT IS 32.544 s at the locked k_b=160 - 1.378x the 23.61 s prediction (commit 83f2a68, capture stream_20261115_233709, start TPU 25.0 C vs a 25.3 C gate, so table-grade). 2 chunks x 160 GPU blocks x 20 NPU blocks: 2/2 published, 2/2 consumed, 1440/1440 executes, 10/10 zero-copy imports, 0 NaN (sampled - see below), wall 80.1 s, GPU block 202.1 ms median over n=320 (702.5 GOPS), one-closure same-route 166.2 ms (854.3 GOPS), NPU block 392.8 ms over n=40, chunk windows 7.93/7.86 s, GPU drift -0.34% over 64.7 s.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5a_decomposition: The 8.93 s overshoot decomposes exactly: 160 x (0.1662 - 0.1474) = 3.01 s of zero-copy import penalty + 160 x (0.2021 - 0.1662) = 5.74 s of per-GEMM closure barriers, leaving 0.18 s residual. The closure term is the bigger half and it is pure engineering waste, not physics.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5a_cheapest_win: The one-closure form of the SAME route costs 166.2 ms against 202.1 ms for 10 per-GEMM closures, so converting the pipeline to one closure per block recovers 5.74 s of the 32.54 s period - 17.6% - without touching the memory model. CAVEAT before promising it: the 166.2 ms figure is labelled a 'reference form' (TSC|gpu); confirm it actually dispatches all 10 GEMMs rather than one, or the 5.7 s is an extrapolation.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5a_solver: solve_cut.py on the measured pairs gives k_b* = 157 (T_G 0.1662) / 150 (0.2021), i.e. even at the current cadence the optimum is k=150 with a 30.26 s period, 2.3 s better than running the locked k=160. Reported, NOT applied - rates_preset_a.json stays locked until the closure question is settled, because fixing closures changes T_G again.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5a_verification_now_sampled: --hash-every 20 cut the verifier from 3.42 s to 0.17 s per 2-chunk run, which is the right trade - but it means '0 NaN words' now covers 2 of 40 blocks, not 40. Either state the sampling rate wherever the guarantee is quoted, or use a strided digest (hash every 64th word of every block: 13.76 MB/64 = 215 KB = ~1.3 ms/block at the measured 170 MB/s) which restores full-block coverage for free. Do not let 'verified' quietly become 'spot-checked'.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5_sustained_stream: 10 chunks x 160 GPU x 20 NPU on the phone, table-grade start (25.0 vs 25.5 C gate): 10/10 published, 10/10 consumed, 7200/7200 executes, wall 370.4 s, 0 fatal, 0 NaN (sampled). Steady-state period 32.72 s over chunks 2-7, so P3.5a's 32.544 s was NOT startup. NPU overlap 90.02% = the (N-1)/N ceiling for N=10, i.e. the coordinator costs nothing; the GPU is the long pole by 4.13x. Handoff 0.51 us mean / 1.14 max; back-pressure 2 us max. Evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_stream_p35.md, capture stream_20261116_000415.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5_GPU_DERATES: THE GPU DOES NOT HOLD ITS RATE. The Mali block goes 203.0 -> 274.2 ms/block (+35.1%) starting at block ~1135 (~230 s of continuous GPU work): a STEP with no recovery, and it clears with cooldown, so it is thermal state, not wear. The NPU stays flat (396.5 -> 394.0 ms). A post-stream one-closure pass measured 251.2 ms against 166.2 ms cold, so the derate is engine-wide, not closure-specific. Every cold-start T_G in this lock is therefore a COLD-START number: the sustained period is 43.87 s at k_b=160, or 37.85 s at the re-solved k_b=138 (T_G 0.2742). Reported, locks on rates untouched.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5_npu_gains_relatively: Because only the GPU derates, the NPU looks better under sustained load, not worse: T_N/T_G goes 3.21 cold -> 2.36 derated, and k_b* falls 150-157 -> 138. The heterogeneous split is MORE valuable in the sustained regime, which is the regime a real deployment lives in.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5_derate_shape_clue: The penalty is not a uniform percentage: 1.351x on the one-closure form would give 224.5 ms, but it measured 251.2 (+51%). Additive is closer (+71 ms for 10 closures vs +85 ms for one) but not exact. A compute-clock throttle scales multiplicatively; a bandwidth / weight-streaming cap hits the more compute-efficient form harder - which is the shape observed. That points at the memory path, the same place the unresolved 'import penalty' lives, so the two anomalies may be one phenomenon. Test on the next run, not by argument.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5_next_diagnosis: No readable GPU clock, so separate DVFS from a thermal trip by logging ALL thermal zones every block during a 10-chunk run and finding which zone crosses a threshold at block ~1135. Then a pure-GPU soak and a pure-NPU soak of 250 s+ would tell whether the trip is engine-specific or device-wide - the NPU staying flat already argues engine-specific.
phase3_pipeline.p3_5_reporting_gap: 'Run average 35.6 s' needs a definition: wall/chunk is 370.4/10 = 37.04 s, so 35.6 must exclude setup and/or chunk 1 - state which. The chain the paper should carry is 23.61 predicted -> 32.72 measured cold -> 43.87 sustained at k=160 -> 37.85 sustained at k=138; quoting any one of those without the thermal state it belongs to is misleading.

npu_constraints.reduction_dim_note: one FULLY_CONNECTED [N=1536,K] compiles at K=1280/1536/1600/1664 (0.34-0.52 s) and fails OP_FAILED from K=1792 up (46-59 s; K=8960 also gave DEAD_OBJECT after 62 s). ffn.up - the same 13.7 MB of weights at K=1536 - compiles in 1.44 s, so the ceiling is the reduction dim, not N or weight bytes. The support query reports every one of those shapes 'supported', so it is not a viability test. Chunk to <=1664, one compilation per op (ffn.down = 7x FC[1536,1280] + 6x ADD, 2.57 s total); chunking inside a single graph does NOT work (down2 = 2x K=4480 + ADD, all ops supported, compile OP_FAILED at 47.8 s).
npu_constraints.graph_shape: one graph per (block, token-tile); whole-block graphs validated and were SUPPORTED by google-edgetpu but Compilation_finish REBOOTED THE DEVICE (2026-11-15) -> one graph per GEMM is the only viable path
npu_constraints.weight_scales: per-tensor only: TENSOR_QUANT8_SYMM_PER_CHANNEL is rejected by FULLY_CONNECTED with addOperation BAD_DATA(4), so the per-output-column scheme cannot be expressed on the NPU stage. DECISION PENDING, but no longer a guess - the cost is measured on the real checkpoint (docs/device/RESULTS_scales.md, 40 GEMM instances = blocks 0/5/15/29 x 10): per-tensor costs 2.15x the mean GEMM output error (3.01% vs 1.40%; median-of-ratios 1.74x, worst 5.44x) and breaks the Gate-1 cosine>=0.999 bar on 6/40 outputs (worst 0.996820), where per-column breaks 0/40 (min 0.999926). The penalty is a WEIGHT property, not a shape property: it tracks per-column scale spread at r=0.805 (per-column error vs spread r=0.101), so a shape-based restriction is unsupportable; the only defensible restriction is per-tensor-where-cheap, attn2.to_k + attn2.to_v = 10.2% of block MACs, leaving 89.8% of block MACs unable to use the NPU under the locked quantisation.
npu_constraints.uncompilable_shape: FC with K=8960 (ffn.down) -> OP_FAILED at 47.2 s / DEAD_OBJECT at 62.0 s, reproduced in fresh processes; it is the K>1664 ceiling, not this shape (see reduction_dim_ceiling). Both workarounds are now MEASURED: chunked 7x FC[1536,1280] + 6x ADD on the TPU = 0.2580 s/block (163.9 GOPS); Mali tiled = 0.04733 s/block (893 GOPS) -> the TPU is 5.45x slower for this GEMM. Engineering recommendation: ffn.down on Mali whichever way the cut lands; the decision is the student's
npu_constraints.conv2d_batch_ceiling: CONV_2D compiles with a batch dim only while the per-frame input is small: N=3 at 0.78 MB/frame compiles in 141.6 ms; N=5/N=3 at 1.4 MB/frame and N=3/N=9 at 6.3 MB/frame grind 31-36 s in Compilation_finish and fail, while the same 37.6 MB tensor compiles in 263 ms at N=1. getSupportedOperationsForDevices reports these shapes delegated=1 and is again not a viability test. Decompose on the frame axis: one execute per frame per temporal tap.
